# dlapy2

> Returns sqrt(x.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlapy2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlapy2';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlapy2( x, y ) → number
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `x` | `number` | First value |
| `y` | `number` | Second value |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `y`: X and Y specify the values x and y.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: result

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlapy2.ndarray( x, y ) → number
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `x` | `number` | First value |
| `y` | `number` | Second value |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `y`: X and Y specify the values x and y.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: sqrt(x\*\*2 + y\*\*2)

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlapy2()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLAPY2`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlapy2.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import dlapy2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlapy2';

// Using the standard interface:
let out = dlapy2( 1, 1 );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = dlapy2.ndarray( 1, 1 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLAPY2`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLAPY2 returns $\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$, taking care not to cause unnecessary overflow and unnecessary underflow.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
